title: Is 9.70 ± 0.04 consistent with 9.81?
caption: The difference is z = (9.81 − 9.70) / 0.04 = 2.75 standard uncertainties. The two tails beyond ±2.75, too thin to see, hold p ≈ 0.006 of the distribution, far below 0.05, so the result is inconsistent: look for a systematic error.
alt: Standard normal curve with a line at z = 2.75 and dashed lines at ±1.96.
description: The curve is the standard normal distribution of z, the difference in units of the standard uncertainty.
Dashed lines at ±1.96 mark the 5% two-sided threshold.
The measurement sits at z = 2.75; the tails beyond ±2.75 together hold p ≈ 0.006.
Since p < 0.05, reject the hypothesis that the measurement agrees with 9.81 m s⁻².
